title: Retirement income and health insurance bundled in AIA-Allianz Retire+ deal
full_text:
Three in four Australian pre-retirees find the range of superannuation retirement income products confusing, and only 6% of retirees currently use a lifetime income product, according to the Super Members Council's (SMC) Retirement Revolution report released in October 2025. A new strategic partnership between AIA Australia and Allianz Australia Life Insurance (Allianz Retire+) aims to address that gap by combining health and wellbeing expertise with guaranteed lifetime income solutions as more than 2.8 million Australians prepare to retire over the next decade.
Under the partnership, AIA will bring its behavioural science-backed health and wellbeing programs – including AIA Vitality, which rewards people for making healthier choices – while Allianz Retire+ will contribute its Allianz Guaranteed Income for Life (AGILE) retirement income solution. The two insurers will work with superannuation funds, wealth platforms, financial advisers, and retirement service providers to deliver what they describe as a connected experience across a lifecycle framework: Engage → Protect → Recover → Prepare → Retire.
For brokers and financial advisers working in the life and health insurance space, the partnership creates a combined proposition where two separate conversations previously existed. An adviser discussing longevity risk with a client nearing retirement can now introduce both a guaranteed income stream and a wellbeing program designed to keep retirees healthier and more engaged, delivered through a single partnership rather than separate provider relationships.
The arrangement is not a product bundle or a cross-referral between health insurance and retirement income. Instead, it pairs AIA’s engagement and wellbeing capability with Allianz Retire+’s decumulation expertise, giving advisers an integrated narrative when working with clients approaching or already in retirement.
Damien Mu, chief executive of AIA Australia, said the partnership reflects a broader view of what retirement planning requires. “At AIA, we are focused on helping people live healthier, longer, better lives. We know that people are currently living longer, but they’re not necessarily spending their later years in good health; and financial security plays a big part in someone’s overall wellbeing. We bring our expertise in lifelong engagement and wellbeing to the table, to combine with the Allianz Retire+ market-leading retirement income guarantee,” Mu said.
David Kane, chief executive of Allianz Retire+ in Sydney, said the partnership builds on growing adviser and fund interest in retirement income solutions. “Allianz Retire+ is experiencing positive momentum as advisers, superannuation funds, and retirees increasingly recognise the value of retirement income solutions, including Allianz Guaranteed Income for Life (AGILE). By bringing together Allianz Retire+’s retirement income expertise and AIA Australia’s strengths in health, wellbeing, and customer engagement, we can help more Australians retire with confidence and achieve better retirement outcomes,” Kane said.
The SMC report estimated that a typical new retiree who fails to optimise their drawdown strategy could forgo as much as $136,000 over the course of retirement, or roughly $6,500 a year. It also found that 41% of pre-retirees find the rules for withdrawing money from super difficult to understand.
Separate research from the AMP Retirement Confidence Pulse, published in September 2026 and based on a Dynata survey of 2,000 Australians, found that 58% worry about running out of money in retirement.
The Financial Advice Association of Australia (FAAA) has pointed to the gap between advised and unadvised Australians as evidence that professional guidance makes a measurable difference. The FAAA’s Value of Advice Index, published in October 2025 and based on a survey of 1,226 respondents, found that 88% of advised Australians believe they will have sufficient funds for retirement, compared with 62% of those without advice.

The AIA-Allianz Retire+ partnership sits within a broader industry move toward integrating accumulation, decumulation and wellbeing solutions. The Australian Prudential Regulation Authority (APRA) has been pushing superannuation trustees to develop comprehensive retirement income strategies under the Retirement Income Covenant, which took effect in July 2022, and Treasury's best practice principles released in late 2024 raised expectations that funds would offer integrated solutions rather than standalone accumulation products.

As longer lifespans put new pressure on Australia’s life insurance market, the question for advisers is whether partnerships like this one genuinely simplify the retirement conversation or add complexity. With retirement income product uptake still in single figures and the research consistently showing that retirees struggle to convert savings into sustainable income, the demand for integrated approaches is clear. How well this particular partnership serves advisers will depend on the operational detail – including platform access, eligibility criteria, and how the wellbeing programs are delivered alongside AGILE – as AIA and Allianz Retire+ roll out the arrangement.
